findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, snapshots and backups holding application data are stored unencrypted.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database directly to untrusted networks and greatly expanding attack surface (only the security group then stands between the DB and the internet).

The master password is supplied through var.password and the same value is interpolated into EC2 user data; combined with the hard-coded 'admin' master username this creates a predictable, exposed credential pair for an internet-reachable database.

The database master password (var.password) is interpolated into the instance user_data script, which is stored unencrypted in the EC2 instance metadata service and readable by any process or compromised application on the host (and via SSRF), and is also written to the Terraform state.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the web instance profile; any compromise of the internet-facing PHP application yields near-administrative control over all S3 data, EC2 (including instance/role manipulation for privilege escalation) and RDS in the account.

No parameter or option enforces TLS for client connections (e.g. require_secure_transport) and the PHP client connects with plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data traverse the network unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, leaving unencrypted database connections permitted.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

The attached ingress rule allows TCP/3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database; combined with publicly_accessible = true this security group is the sole boundary for the database.

The instance defines no root_block_device with encrypted = true and no metadata_options enforcing http_tokens = "required", so the EBS volume is unencrypted and IMDSv1 remains enabled, allowing SSRF in the PHP application to retrieve the highly privileged role credentials.

The instance is placed in a subnet and outputs a public DNS name, serving an unauthenticated PHP page over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS configured), so application traffic and any submitted data travel in cleartext on a directly reachable host.
